label: Multi-machine Git task-state guard
description: Defines the non-mutating checks required before starting, finishing, rescuing, or merging Codex/AIDE task work across machines.
pass_conditions: working tree is clean for start-task, finish-task, and merge-task modes
no active merge, rebase, cherry-pick, or revert metadata exists
normal task work runs on a named non-main task branch
local main is current with origin/main or can fast-forward from it before task work begins
task branch is not behind its upstream
no staged or untracked secret-like or private local paths are present
warn_conditions: task branch has no upstream before first push
branch name does not include the task ID
AIDE queue stale relative to git log
AIDE context appears stale relative to git log
origin/main advanced since task packet generation
task branch has local commits that still need a normal push
origin/main is unavailable in a local-only test repository
fail_conditions: local main behind origin/main when starting task work
current branch is main for normal task work
local main has merge commits that have not been pushed to origin/main
allowed_overrides: --allow-main for explicit integration, rescue, or repo sync guard work
--allow-no-upstream for a new branch before its first push
--expected-origin-main to warn when remote-tracking state differs from packet context
--fail-on-warn for CI or strict operator gates
notes: The guard inspects local Git state only by default.
Fetching is an explicit workflow step, not a guard side effect.
WARN means the operator can proceed only after acknowledging the listed condition.
